newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Report SAfrica's Mandela threatened to quit denied.
newsitem.headline: Report SAfrica's Mandela threatened to quit denied.

text.p: Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana denied a newspaper report on Friday that Nelson Mandela had threatened to resign following a showdown with the South African Communist Party (SACP) over economic policy.

The Star said in a front page report that Mandela was so angry with SACP deputy secretary general Jeremy Cronin for criticising the African National Congress (ANC) in public over privatisation that he threatened to quit unless Cronin was fired.
But Mankahlana told Reuters: "The president did not threaten to resign either as president of the ANC or as president of the country."

Cronin, an ANC member, has been a vocal critic of the government's market-orientated economic policy outlined in the government's five-year macro-economic strategy unveiled in June, which includes a commitment to privatisation.

Party sources said the issue came to a head at a recent meeting of the the ANC's national executive committee (NEC). The SACP is an ally of the ANC alongside labour unions in the triple alliance which swept Mandela to power in 1994.
One ANC source said Mandela told the NEC that the macro-economic strategy had to be accepted by all members and could not be rejected by some within the ranks of the party.

The source added: "The president said you cannot be a member of the ANC and then when you don't like what is happening criticise as a member of the Communist Party or of Cosatu (Congress of South Africa Trade Unions)."
Mandela made it clear that those who could not support the strategy would have to find another political home -- ANC members had a duty to align themselves behind official policy of the party.
